mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer confidence and residential investment, which typically precedes higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST increases by more than 2% in the prior month but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 3.0% in a sustained manner, it signals a tightening monetary policy that reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of the 5-day periods following the threshold crossing.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market that fuels consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining UNRATE and rising PAYEMS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression has a negative coefficient.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve's focus on inflation control leads to higher real interest rates, which depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the regime-specific signal has a Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE declines by more than 0.2 percentage points in the prior month but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0 (index 2017=100), it signals a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain disruptions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO drops below 105.0 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of the 5-day periods following the drop.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and decline in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates strong consumer demand coupled with accommodative monetary policy, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising RSAFS and falling FEDFUNDS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) exceeds 2.5% annualized, it signals a late-cycle expansion where the economy is near full capacity, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% annualized, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the signal has a Rank IC < 0.03.
